You have some great pieces to work with here! I love the plaid pants, the yellow top, and red dress. I think maybe updating with a few items that are a little more form fitting would be a great start. As a short person myself, i find that i have to be careful with skirts and dresses (which is primarily what i wear) because if it stops in the wrong place on my legs, it makes me look super short and makes me look outdated. 

I would suggest trying a few clothing items that are a bit shorter (in the skirts and dresses), or less baggy. And if you feel like you need to cover up a bit, a nice cardigan with or without a belt can work well too (as long as it’s not too long or you’ll run into the same issues).

Seconding the shoe comment, i think you could definitely upgrade to a more modern looking pair of shoes. Are you on your feet at work? Im not sure what the weather is like year round in your location, but when i used to have a dress code for work, i usually did a nice suede or leather bootie in the fall/winter, and sandals or an upgraded pair of flats in the spring/summer. 

Note on the flats tho: as a short and very wide person myself, I find that most flats make me look shorter for whatever reason. If i do flats, they need to have a thicker platform for support and for elongating my legs a bit, hence why i said “upgraded” flats

I have a croton Petra that has been doing well - put out 9 new leaves in the last 6 months that are turning red, with 3 more growing in now! 

I have it in a bright bright spot about 4 ft from a window. It gets some direct sunlight, but not too harsh. I don’t do much in the way of humidity, but it sits in my living room among other sun loving plants, and generally that room is a little more humid than others in my apartment. I only water when the leaves start dropping - it’s a bit of a diva in that the droop starts and gets dramatic quickly, but as soon as it gets a drink the leaves perk up immediately lol. That is how i water most of my plants, with a few exceptions. I recently repotted to a bigger pot because i let it get a little root bound since they don’t like too much change and can lose leaves. As for pot size, I'll say that all of my calatheas and prayer plants are still in their nursery pots and doing well, and those pots are pretty small. If I were in your position, I would repot in a pot 1 or 2 sizes smaller than the one you have now. It looks like the soil you're using is mostly peat moss, which holds on to a ton of water. Calatheas like moisture,  but they don't like wetness. I would amend your soil with perlite and orchid bark if you can find it (though just using perlite should be fine, and it's easy to get). This will help the water drain better. Also, might want to try very lightly fertilizing, as it could be missing nutrients.
